To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a voltage doubler-type rectenna has a high conversion efficiency at a large output load, and the improvement of conversion efficiency is dependent on the electric discharge time and the microwave period.

the VD-type and the HWR-type rectenna show VD behavior without a charge pump capacitor, and the improvement of the rectifier efficiency of the VD-type to the HWR-type is caused by the electric charge stored and discharged in the junction and packaging capacitances of the rectenna.

the developed VD type rectenna showed drastic improvement to the RF–dc efficiency in comparison with the HWR type rectenna at output load exceeding  $100 \Omega$  because the VD type rectennas show voltage doubler behavior even without the charge-pump capacitor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the VD-type RF–dc conversion circuit and its application to rectennas.
the VD behavior of a 1.5-GHz VD rectenna.
the VD behavior of the VD- type rectenna, and the improvement of the VD-type RF–dc conversion performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the developed VD rectenna is a VD that does not have a charge pump capacitor.
the VD-type RF–dc converter is a VD that does not use a charge pump capacitor.

the VD-type diode rectenna shows a higher RF–dc conversion at higher loads than a HWR-type rectenna because the diode junction and package capacitance act as an electric charge storage device and a dc voltage conservation mechanism, respectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the developed VD rectenna can be used to improve the RF–dc efficiency in comparison with the HWR rectenna.
the VD-type diode rectenna is superior in RF–dc conversion performance to the conventional HWR-type rectenna.
the developed rectenna is suitable for a dc power source for a wireless sensor network.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the VD-type circuit is suitable for RF–dc conversion when the input microwave period is comparable to the electric discharge time constants of the rectenna.
the developed VD- and the HWR-type rectenna are VD-type rectennas, even though they do not have a charge pump capacitor.
the VD-type circuit can improve the RF–dc efficiency at output loads exceeding $100~\text{Ω} $ by conserving the dc voltage even at the input microwave negative voltage.
